description: The Earth Ox in Chinese astrology: personality, Earth element traits, 1949 and 2009 dates and compatibility.
answer: In Chinese astrology, the Earth Ox is the Ox born in a Earth year, one of five versions of the second animal. It combines the Ox's patience with Earth's qualities. Earth Ox years between 1924 and 2044 are 1949 and 2009. The Ox's fixed element is Earth.

sections.heading: The Earth Ox personality
paragraphs: In the Earth Ox, the year stem and the animal's fixed element are the same, since the Ox always carries Earth. Traditional readings treat this as the Ox in its purest form: patient, methodical, honest and enormously reliable. Earth Oxen are often described as people who build slowly and well, whose word can be trusted and whose loyalty, once given, rarely wavers. They tend to be practical, frugal and attuned to the rhythms of hard work. The doubled Earth gives them exceptional endurance and a calm presence in a crisis. It can also make them heavy, slow to adapt and inclined to carry worries privately, assuming no one else could shoulder the load as well.

Earth sits at the centre of the five-element wheel, and an Earth year is traditionally said to give any animal steadiness, patience and a practical turn of mind. Descriptions associate it with reliability, honesty and a talent for holding things together, whether that means a family, a budget or a team in a difficult season. Earth-year people are often portrayed as grounded, fair and good at turning ideas into workable plans. The element is linked with nourishment and care, so it carries a quiet generosity. Its shadow, in most readings, is heaviness: worry, stubbornness and a reluctance to move until every risk has been weighed twice.

sections.heading: Earth Ox at work and in love
paragraphs: At work, Earth is usually associated with management, organisation and long-term stewardship. Earth-year people are often described as the steady hands who keep systems running, look after budgets and notice when colleagues are struggling, which suits administration, property, finance, agriculture, healthcare and operations. They tend to earn trust slowly and keep it. The traditional caution is resistance to change: an Earth stem may hold on to a process after it has stopped working, so regular reviews and a willingness to experiment help.

The Earth Ox is the craftsperson of the zodiac, content to spend years perfecting a skill that others would drop after a season. Banking, civil engineering, farming, archiving, joinery and quality control are frequently mentioned, since each prizes accuracy over flair. Clear processes, fair pay and a boss who keeps promises suit it; office politics simply bore it. In a long partnership the Earth Ox offers constancy measured in decades rather than gestures, from the same anniversary restaurant to the car serviced before every holiday. Honesty, routine and a settled home are what it asks in return. Loved ones sometimes wish for more spoken warmth, and the old sticking point is rigidity, especially when plans change at short notice.

sections.heading: Earth Ox years and dates
paragraphs: Between 1924 and 2044 the Earth Ox years are 1949 (January 29, 1949 to February 16, 1950) and 2009 (January 26, 2009 to February 13, 2010). Because the year begins at Lunar New Year, a birthday in January or early February needs checking: in 1949 anyone born before Jan 29 is a Earth Rat, not a Earth Ox. The combination returns every sixty years, since five elements cycle through twelve animals and only meet the same pairing again after five rounds of the zodiac. Every Earth Ox year is Yin, matching the Ox's own polarity.

Chinese almanacs call the combination Ji-Chou, joining the heavenly stem Ji to the earthly branch Chou. Births just before each new year fall in the Earth Rat year (before January 29, 1949) and the Earth Rat year (before January 26, 2009), and births in the weeks after each Earth Ox year ends belong to the Metal Tiger. The new year itself fell on a Saturday in 1949 and Monday in 2009.

sections.heading: Growth edges and compatibility for the Earth Ox
paragraphs: The growth edge for the Earth Ox is movement. Readings suggest that this deeply grounded combination benefits from deliberate novelty, new places, new friendships, new ways of doing familiar tasks, so that stability does not harden into a rut. Earth Oxen may also struggle to express affection in words; small verbal acknowledgements can mean a great deal to the people around them. Because they carry responsibility so naturally, learning to delegate is important. Light exercise, music and play tend to lift the heaviness that doubled Earth can bring. When they allow some lightness in, Earth Oxen become the most reassuring presence in any room.

For relationships, the classical structures belong to the animal rather than the element, so the Earth Ox shares the Ox's San He trine with the Snake and Rooster (the Metal trine), its Liu He bond with the Rat, and its Liu Chong clash with the Goat. The element adds a second layer: another Earth sign shares this year element, while partners whose year element feeds Earth in the generating cycle are often described as supportive.

faq.question: What years are Earth Ox years?
faq.answer: Between 1924 and 2044: 1949 (from January 29, 1949) and 2009 (from January 26, 2009). Each lasts until the day before the next Lunar New Year.

faq.question: What is the Earth Ox's element relationship?
faq.answer: The year element is Earth and the Ox's fixed element is Earth; in the five-element cycles earth year element matches the fixed element. Readings use that relationship to describe how easily the two sides of the sign sit together.

faq.question: Which animals are most compatible with the Earth Ox?
faq.answer: Traditionally the Snake and Rooster (San He) and the Rat (Liu He). The Goat is the Liu Chong clash. These pairings depend on the animal, whatever the element.

faq.question: What is the Earth Ox called in the Chinese calendar?
faq.answer: Ji-Chou. In almanacs and Four Pillars charts each year is named by its heavenly stem, here the Earth stem Ji, followed by its earthly branch, here Chou for the Ox, so the name pins down both halves of the combination at once.

faq.question: How is the Earth Ox different from other Oxs?
faq.answer: All Oxs share patience, diligence and steady strength. The Earth year element changes the tone: earth sits at the centre of the five-element wheel, and an Earth year is traditionally said to give any animal steadiness, patience and a practical turn of mind.
